title: Respond to a government subpoena or data request
summary: Record the issuer, scope, deadline and confidentiality terms of the government demand. Preserve relevant records separately from disclosure, obtain counsel’s review of validity and permitted notice, and make only the authorized response through the applicable legal process.

countryViews.title: Respond to a government subpoena or data request in United States
countryViews.summary: Legal process about your users arrives like ordinary mail and binds like none of it. Read the demand first: who issued it, which instrument it is (subpoena, court order, or warrant reach different data under the Stored Communications Act's tiers, law rule us-fed.sca-provider-disclosure), exactly what it names, the printed deadline, and whether a nondisclosure order rides with it. Preserve immediately and separately from producing: a § 2703(f) request obliges a provider to hold the named records for 90 days, renewable once on a renewed request (law rule us-fed.sca-preservation-request). Counsel reviews scope and validity before anything goes out, because voluntary disclosure of content outside the statutory exceptions is prohibited. Whether you may tell the affected user depends on the paperwork: a court can command silence on the § 2705(b) findings (law rule us-fed.sca-notice-preclusion), and absent such an order your own published law-enforcement guidelines and notice promises govern. Produce exactly what the process compels, record what went out, and check the vendor layer, because your processors and hosts receive demands about your users too. Educational guidance, not legal advice; the demand's own text and counsel control every step here.

parts.title: Read the demand: issuer, instrument type, exactly what it names, the printed deadline, and any nondisclosure order attached

execution.rationale: Extract the issuer, instrument, named accounts, deadline, and any sealing language from the supplied demand for counsel's review.

parts.title: Draft the preservation hold now, separately from producing: exactly what the demand names, the deletion jobs to suspend, and the hold log
parts.guidance: Preserve the records covered by the demand while counsel verifies the applicable scope and retention period. Suspend relevant deletion jobs, document the hold and distinguish preservation from disclosure.

execution.rationale: Draft the hold scope, the list of retention jobs to suspend, and the hold log from the demand's own terms; the changes to live retention systems are the system owners' acts on that draft.

geoResolutions.label: The preservation duty on request is statutory: 90 days, renewable once on a renewed request (law rule us-fed.sca-preservation-request)
geoResolutions.guidance: Preservation and production are different acts. A § 2703(f) preservation request obliges a provider to take all necessary steps to preserve the named records for 90 days, extended another 90 on a renewed request, pending legal process (law rule us-fed.sca-preservation-request). Holding the data is not disclosing it; scope the hold to exactly what the demand names. The system owners place the holds and suspend the retention jobs in the live systems from this draft, and the log records what they did and when.

parts.title: Counsel before production or reply: scope, validity, and which instrument reaches which data
parts.guidance: Have counsel assess the issuer’s authority, the legal instrument, the requested data and applicable disclosure restrictions. Resolve scope or validity questions through the authorized process before the response deadline.

execution.rationale: Counsel reads the demand against the statute and negotiates scope with the issuer; validity and narrowing are legal judgment on live facts.

geoResolutions.label: Counsel before production or reply: scope, validity, and which instrument reaches which data
geoResolutions.guidance: A provider shall not voluntarily divulge the contents of communications outside the statutory exceptions, and compelled disclosure runs through the warrant, court-order, and subpoena tiers, which reach different classes of data (law rule us-fed.sca-provider-disclosure). Overbreadth, the wrong instrument for the data sought, and jurisdiction are counsel questions, raised with the issuer before the deadline rather than discovered after production.

parts.title: Decide whether user notice is permitted and required with counsel
parts.guidance: Have counsel determine whether the demand, an accompanying order or applicable law restricts notice. Consider the company’s published commitments and record the authorized notice decision and its basis.

references.title: 18 U.S.C. § 2705 — delayed notice and preclusion orders

execution.rationale: Counsel reads the order and the company's own notice commitments; telling or not telling a user is a consequential human decision under legal constraint.

geoResolutions.label: Decide user notice with counsel: a § 2705(b) order commands silence; without one, your published guidelines and promises govern
geoResolutions.guidance: A court may order the provider not to notify anyone of the demand's existence, for the period the court sets, on the § 2705(b) findings (law rule us-fed.sca-notice-preclusion). Absent such an order or another sealing obligation, the statute does not itself forbid notifying the affected user; what you promised in your privacy policy and law-enforcement guidelines, and what counsel advises on the specific demand, decide the call. Record the decision and its basis either way.
geoResolutions.actionLabel: 18 U.S.C. § 2705 — delayed notice and preclusion orders

parts.title: Produce exactly what the process compels, through counsel, by the deadline, and record what was produced

execution.rationale: Counsel transmits the production and any required certification; an over-production cannot be recalled, so the final review and the send are human acts.

parts.title: Check the vendor layer: your processors and hosts receive legal process about your users too, so know their notice policies
parts.guidance: The same demand, or a parallel one, can land at your payment processor, cloud host, or email provider. Read each major vendor's law-enforcement guidelines for whether and when they notify customers of process about customer data, and note which vendors would tell you and which would not.

execution.rationale: Compile the notice positions from the vendors' published law-enforcement guidelines into one reference for counsel and the on-call owner.

metadata.trigger: A government subpoena, court order, or warrant arrives demanding user data or company records, sometimes with a nondisclosure order attached.
metadata.supportReason: Scope, validity, and the notice decision are counsel work; an agent can extract the demand's terms, place and log the preservation hold, and compile the vendors' published notice positions.

your published privacy policy and any law-enforcement guidelines with notice promises
